newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia stocks end down on certification doubts.
newsitem.headline: Colombia stocks end down on certification doubts.

text.p: Colombian stocks drifted down amid investor fears about the implications of a possible decision by the United States to "decertify" Colombia for a second consecutive year.
Bogota's IBB index dipped 0.01 percent to 1,068.64 amid a 1.8 billion peso volume while Medellin's IBOMED index dropped 0.23 percent to 16,733.21 amid a 2.3 billion peso volume.

The United States is due to announce whther it will "certify" or balcklist Colombia for its anti-drug efforts before the weekend. Renewed decertification could trigger economic sanctions, U.S. officials have warned.
"Some large clients are taking profits because they expect sanctions to be imposed. Other investors are just not buying until they see what happens," a Bogota broker said.
One of the biggest fallers was Banco de Bogota, down 2.14 percent to 6,400 on the Bogota exchange and down 2.31 percent to 6,399 in Medellin.
A Medellin broker, however, rejected that the looming certification decision was driving down prices and said the falls came on the back of prearranged cross deals.
In Bogota, Banco de Colombia fell 0.22 percent to 435 pesos while in Medellin it fell back 1.14 percent to the same price.
Brewing giant Bavaria fell 0.43 percent in Bogota to 6,870 and 1.45 percent in Medellin to 6,800.
Cement manufacturer Cemento Argos, part of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate, dropped 0.39 percent on both exchanges to 7,600 pesos.
Falls in the IBB were offset by gains in Banco Ganadero. Its ordinary shares gained 0.9 percent to 333 and its preferential shares rose 7.43 percent.
A cross deal in Cementos Paz del Rio rose 1.07 percent to 940 pesos.
